transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess things have just been... a bit much lately. 

I just keep feeling like I really let my family down with this mortgage I took on. And... I don't know. Even at work, every little mistake I make just kind of... proves I'm useless. Like I just deserve whatever happens to me. 

So... yeah. I guess that's why I'm here.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?
Um... well, the... the really low parts, feeling like a failure and all that... it's been a while. Maybe... a year? A little over a year, I think. Like 14 months or so, total.

Over this past year or so, have you been feeling this way pretty much every day, most of the day, without breaks—or have there been stretches of weeks or months where you felt back to your normal self in between?

Um... not really any long breaks, no. Most of this whole time... even if some days were a little lighter... I've just been weighed down by it. That... empty, guilty feeling. It's just there more often than not.
During this past year, has there been a stretch of at least two weeks where your mood, energy, sleep, or interest in things got noticeably worse than your usual baseline?

Um... yeah, I guess so. It's just... most days there's this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. Like... I go to work, I carry plates to tables, and I smile at people because I'm supposed to. Not because I actually feel anything good. It just... it doesn't really go away.

During this past year, was there a stretch of at least two weeks when things got much worse—where you also noticed big changes in your sleep, appetite, concentration, or even thoughts of not wanting to be alive—compared to how you'd been feeling the rest of the time?
Um... I don't know. It all just... kind of blends together. I haven't really kept track of... specific weeks being worse than others. It's just... mostly the same.
Right now, do you find that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with people?
Um... I guess so. I don't really do much anymore. Just... go to work and come home. There's not really anything I want to do.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep recently—like trouble falling asleep, waking up often, or sleeping much more or less than usual?
Um... no, not really. Sleep is... just sleep. I guess I get enough. It hasn't really changed.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over the past year—eating much more or less than usual, or gaining or losing weight without trying?

Um... I guess my eating is kind of... all over the place. Like... sometimes at work I barely touch the staff meal. But then... other nights I'll get home and just... eat whatever is in the kitchen. I don't know, just... to feel settled, I guess.
During this past year, have you ever had thoughts of death, of not wanting to be alive, or of harming yourself?

Um... I mean, I don't... I wouldn't actually do anything to hurt myself. I don't have a plan or anything like that. But... sometimes, when I'm just lying there before an early shift... I don't know. I just think... maybe it would be easier if I didn't wake up. Then I wouldn't have to... keep messing everything up. But I wouldn't actually do anything.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to concentrate or make decisions—like at work or in daily tasks—over this past year?

Um... maybe a little bit. Work has just been... I don't know. Like with the POS system, or... doing the inventory sheets. Sometimes I just have trouble keeping the numbers straight. I'll just... stare at the screen. I've done this for years, but lately I just don't trust that I entered it right. So... yeah. I guess.
Before this past year began, had you ever gone through a similar period of feeling down or empty like this, followed by a stretch of time where you felt completely back to your normal self?
Um... I don't really know. I haven't really thought about it. I mean... I've had times where I felt a little off before, but... I don't remember if it was exactly like this. I just... I don't know.
Over the past year, have you been feeling unusually tired or low on energy most days, even after resting?
Not really. I mean... I'm on my feet all day for work, so I get tired. But... I don't think it's anything unusual. Just normal tired, I guess.
Thinking back further, has this low, empty, guilty feeling been present continuously for at least two years, or did it really start around a year ago?
Um... no, not two years. I think... just around a year ago, I guess. I don't really keep track, but... it hasn't been that long.
Have these feelings and difficulties made it hard for you to keep up with your job, relationships, or daily responsibilities?

I mean... I guess it's been a little tough. I almost missed a couple of shifts recently. And... I messed up some mortgage paperwork. I just... I have a harder time focusing on the POS reports and the inventory at work. I worry a lot about losing my job... and the condo. And I guess I haven't been talking to my brother much, or the people at the restaurant. They... they've mentioned I seem kind of quiet lately. But... I don't know.
Have others noticed you moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or alternatively, have you felt restless or unable to sit still over this past year?

Um... yeah, I guess so. People at work... they've said something about it. Sometimes I pace around a lot... like, checking the same tables and receipts over and over. Or... I just get really slowed down. Like it takes me way longer than it should just to grab menus or walk over to the POS. I don't really know why.
Would you say that, despite the difficulty, you're still able to get through most of your work shifts and daily responsibilities, or has it reached a point where you often can't manage them at all?

I mean... I'm still getting through it, mostly. I haven't actually missed a shift, just... almost. But it's hard. The mistakes with the paperwork and the POS reports... I just worry a lot about losing the job. If I lose the job, I lose the condo. And... I know people notice I'm not myself. I just... I don't really want to talk to my brother or the guys at work right now. But I'm still going in.
{"intent": "Assess overall severity of functional impairment across all areas

I guess... it's just like I said. I've almost missed a couple shifts. I messed up that mortgage paperwork... and I just can't focus on the POS reports or the inventory like I used to. It's just... I worry about getting fired. If I lose the job, the condo goes next. And... I guess I'm just not talking to my brother or the guys at work much. They notice it. They know something's off. But... yeah. I'm still getting by.
Have you ever felt convinced of things that others say aren't true—like feeling certain you're being punished, or hearing or seeing things that others don't seem to notice?

I don't hear things. But... I don't know. I just get this feeling sometimes. Like the bank, or even my manager... like they're watching me. Just waiting for me to screw up. Even when someone points out it was just a normal register error, or a regular paperwork mistake... I just can't shake the feeling.

When you feel like your manager or the bank is watching you, waiting for you to fail—do you genuinely believe that's really happening, even when there's no evidence for it, or does part of you recognize it's probably just your worry talking?

I don't know... I mean, people tell me it's just my worry. They show me the paperwork or the register, and say it was just a normal mistake. But... I just can't shake the feeling. It still feels like they're watching for me to mess up. I just... I can't turn that feeling off.

When you have clear proof it was just a normal mistake, do you still truly believe, deep down, that your manager or the bank are actually watching and waiting for you to fail—or do you know that's probably not really true, even though the worry feeling doesn't go away?
I mean... even with the proof... I still believe it. Deep down. I know what people say, but... it doesn't change anything. I just know they're watching me. Waiting for that slip-up.
